notes:
Quick summary: Elmstone is a mid-market product team building a contextual help & knowledge product embedded in customer apps. Primary goal: reduce live agent load and improve NPS via a chat + document search combo. Evaluating Redwood hosted API first for fast time-to-value; leaning toward Dedicated within Q2 once latency & unit economics are proven. Key shades: cost-sensitive (token-heavy product), cares about tail latency for chat, wants predictable pricing for peak seasonal traffic.

POC/Technical constraints: 80-120 req/s peak expected, p95 chat latency target <= 350ms (p50 target 150-220ms), long-context documents (up to 8k tokens), prefix-heavy prompts for context-loading. Want: KV/prefix caching and batching to shave token cost. Interested in int8/llm.q4 quantized variants but need quality regression checks.

Security/compliance: requires SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration for customer keys. VPC option desired for Dedicated. Security questionnaire submitted 2026-03-01; SOC2 evidence needed for final procurement.

Commercials & pricing convo notes: initial hosted API spend during POC estimated $8k-$12k over 8 weeks (token-heavy). Sales discussed Reserved Dedicated baseline at ~3-5 GPUs equivalent with burst policy; preliminary ARR math shows Dedicated attractive if sustained monthly token volumes > 120M tokens. Ran a quick unit-econ spreadsheet during workshop: with batching + prefix caching we model 30-45% token savings; quantization could reduce Dedicated instance cost by ~20% at potential small quality delta.

Direct quote from CTO: "We like Redwood's routing and rollback story — but need to see real numbers on cost per useful response after caching."

CRM shorthand / friction points: POC success criteria not yet fully aligned w/ finance (ops wants hard $/response). SE asked for a quick microbenchmark (same prompts, hosted vs dedicated quantized) mid-POC.
